items.title: 67246_Buck Clayton oral history interview
items.q: The transcript mentions 'Jonesy' only in the context of a story narrated by Mrs. Clayton about people leaving Shanghai; Buck Clayton (the interviewee) does not speak or provide any personal connection to Jonesy.

ctx.x: Yes. And I, after I told these fellows all of this, I said it's time, I think we should get out. They all had their money then. So everybody left home, I mean left bass man. He stayed there. And as no sooner I left, when I left about less than two weeks, the war exploded. They sent these gun boats right down in the middle of Shanghai and started shooting right into the city.
And everybody got out except Jonesy and he was put in a concentration camp. And he
still, he's out in Los Angeles today, he still has trouble with his legs where they, what they did to him, you know. But, he was in this Japanese camp.
